qt: to the Commission Elissavet Vozemberg-Vrionidi (PPE) Subject:

Greece continues to come under migratory pressure and is eligible to receive support from the Annual Solidarity Pool. This is according to the 2026 European Annual Asylum and Migration Report. While the number of arrivals along the Eastern Mediterranean route has dropped overall, arrivals along the land border shared between Greece and Türkiye went up by 33 % in 2026, accounting for 21 % of all arrivals along this route. Of particular concern is the 105 % increase in arrivals seen in Crete. Meanwhile, the annual Türkiye 2026 Report brings several priorities back to the front burner, including the full implementation of the 2016 EU-Turkey Statement, the resumption of returns from the Greek islands and the full implementation of the 2013 EU-Turkey Readmission Agreement in relation to all EU Member States. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How effective does it consider cooperation with Türkiye to be on preventing irregular crossings and dismantling organised migrant smuggling networks in the Aegean?

What new measures does it intend to take to put further pressure on Türkiye to ensure that it fully honours its commitments under the EU-Turkey Statement and the Readmission Agreement, with a view to effectively addressing the increased pressure on Greek and European borders?
What additional steps will it take to close the existing gaps in the implementation of the New Pact on Migration and Asylum?
